summary: Shipped myiotsan's P4 (actuation & device twin): an admin can now WRITE to a device, not just read it — switching a relay or setting a bounded setpoint, currently for the one shipped profile that declares any command (smart-relay). Every safety gate the plan called for is enforced server-side in the new services.CommandService: read-only by default (a device is refused unless its ActuationEnabled toggle is explicitly on; adoption never sets it), admin-only (a catalog rule written in P0, before the command path existed), only what the device's profile declares (there is no generic publish-to-any-topic endpoint), server-side Min/Max bounds (a setpoint declaring no range at all, Min == Max == 0, refuses every value rather than allowing anything), a 2-second per-device rate limit, and a device_command audit row plus a notification for every attempt including refusals. Two properties the original plan did not name were also built in: a command is NEVER automatically retried after an unconfirmed timeout (30s, swept every 10s) because re-sending a relay write is a second physical action that could fire the relay twice, so a timeout ends the command with an explicit not-retried explanation and leaves the decision to a human (verified live against a relay simulator that obeys but never reports back: the relay physically switched, the command was recorded failed, and exactly one command was ever sent); and the device twin's desired state expires after 5 minutes and is never re-applied when a device reconnects, so a door controller offline for a month does not spring back to life and apply a stale unlock command nobody is around to see — the disagreement is still shown to an operator, just not acted on. A command reaches confirmed only when the device itself reports the resulting state back on the profile's declared confirm key (services.Ingest now feeds every decoded sample into the twin's reported half); sent means only that a message was published, not that anything physically happened, and the API/UI are both built around never conflating the two. Along the way, a real pre-existing gap was found and closed: /api/settings/users and /api/settings/roles had been named in myiotsan's policy catalog since P0, and the viewer/operator roles have existed since then, but nothing served those routes, so both roles were unassignable and the appliance was effectively single-admin; apps/myiotsan/apis/settings.go now serves them on the same shared appliance user service mymatasan uses. Reading a device's command history and its twin is granted to viewer and operator, not just admin, since seeing what was done to a device is not the same power as doing it.
compatibility: New app surface only; myiotsan has no prior installs or deployed fleets to migrate. ActuationEnabled defaults to false for every device (new and pre-existing), so no device becomes commandable without an explicit admin opt-in even on an appliance upgraded in place. Of the eight built-in device-type profiles, only the new smart-relay profile declares a command; every other shipped profile remains read-only exactly as before. Deviates from docs/MYIOTSAN_PLAN.md section 3.4, which specified writing every command to myseliasan's existing audit_log: myiotsan is a standalone appliance that may never be adopted into a myseliasan fleet (fleet adoption is P6, unstarted), so the audit trail is myiotsan's own device_command table plus its notification feed instead; see docs/MYIOTSAN_PLAN.md section 8d for the recorded deviation. mymatasan, myidsan and myseliasan are untouched by this change.
